Authorities say all three suspects, Eddie, Ariel, and Lequinton, are facing the same charges, including conspiracy to commit racketeering, organized retail theft, dealing in stolen property, and one count of unlawful use of a two-way communication device. According to investigators, this case centers around an organized retail theft ring operating across multiple counties in South Florida. Authorities say Eddie played a major role in the operation and was initially on the run before being taken into custody on December 31st, 2024. The investigation began on March 26th after a theft at a Walgreens in West Palm Beach, but quickly expanded as detectives linked the group to more than 35 thefts over a four-month period. Officials say the suspects targeted major retail stores, stealing high-value items such as laundry detergent, luxury fragrances, and designer clothing. Investigators alleged the group worked in a coordinated system, using a vehicle registered to aerial to travel between locations, while others carried out the thefts inside the stores. Authorities also say digital evidence, including cell phone data and financial transactions, showed planning and the resale of stolen items through online platforms, with evidence suggesting involvement in the distribution of controlled substances.
